title: Ultracode slider
description: An effort picker with six levels. Every level is a plain slider stop until the last one: at Ultracode a pixel trail grows from the thumb toward the left, light pulses run along it and a burst fires on arrival.
The label rolls like a picker wheel in the direction of the change. Dragging snaps on a slightly underdamped spring.
tryText: **Try:** drag to Max, then to Ultracode. Use the arrow keys, Home and End.

title: Thinking indicator
description: A pixel wave and a shimmering label while the model works, with a seconds counter that rolls on every tick. When it finishes, the glyph draws a check and the label rolls to “Thought for 6s”, which opens the reasoning.
stage: Effort levels change how long the model reasons. Ultracode is different: it sends xhigh and lets the model plan multi-agent workflows on its own, so the slider should give it its own state rather than another grey step.

title: Send / stop button
description: The arrow launches up and out, a stop square spins in, and a ring orbits while the reply streams. On completion the ring closes, sparks fly and the arrow drops back in.
tryText: **Try:** press send. It completes after 3 s, or press stop to cancel.

title: Toggle
description: The thumb stretches like a drop as it travels, the accent floods out from under it, and a few pixel sparks pop when it switches on. Clicking the label works too.
stage:
Extended thinkingThink longer before answering
Web searchLook up current information

title: Segmented control
description: Two springs drive the selection pill: the leading edge snaps ahead, the trailing edge catches up, so it stretches and squashes on the way. Labels change colour exactly where the pill covers them.
tryText: **Try:** jump from Day to Year, or use the arrow keys.

title: Copy button
description: The clipboard icon spins away as a check draws itself in, the label rolls to “Copied”, and a small pop of pixels confirms it. If the browser refuses the copy, it says so instead.
stage: npx shadcn@latest add @lumesec/ui-copy-button

title: Hold to confirm
description: For destructive actions. Holding fills the button behind a crawling, dithered edge while the bin lid lifts. Let go early and it drains, shakes and asks you to keep holding.
tryText: **Try:** hold for 1.2 s, then try letting go halfway.

title: Odometer stepper
description: Every digit is its own wheel, and changes ripple from the right like a mechanical counter. Columns and the thousands separator slide in when the number gets longer.
tryText: **Try:** hold +, drag sideways on the number, or scroll over it.

title: Toast stack
description: New toasts spring up from below and older ones tuck in behind. Hovering fans the stack out and pauses the timers; swipe a toast sideways to throw it away.
tryText: **Try:** show four or five, hover, then flick one away.

title: Rotary dial
description: Drag around the knob and it follows your pointer, with a click at each detent: the tick flashes, the knob nudges and the value rolls. Let go and it springs onto the nearest step.

title: Context meter
description: Usage fills a strip of pixels behind a glowing front, turns amber past 80 % and red near the limit. Compacting sends a bright band back across the strip as the count drops.

title: Agent workflow
description: Ultracode’s fan-out, drawn live. The planner charges up and bursts, four agent clusters bloom, packets stream along the wires, each agent fills its own pixel ring, and the verifier merges the results into a check.
tryText: **Try:** run it twice. Every agent takes a different amount of time.

title: Throughput gauge
description: Tokens per second on four rings of pixels, with amber and red zones. The needle is a spring, so it overshoots and settles, and a peak marker hangs at the high point before sliding back.
tryText: **Try:** hold the button or the gauge itself to rev it into the red.

title: Rate-limit hourglass
description: A real falling-sand simulation counts down to the next usage reset. Grains pile up, slide off each other and squeeze through the neck one at a time; the timer is how much sand is left.
tryText: **Try:** flip it halfway through and watch the sand run back.

title: Split-flap board
description: A departure board of flip tiles. Each tile flips through the alphabet until it lands on its letter, with the flaps cascading left to right, so status changes feel like an announcement.
tryText: **Try:** click the board to skip ahead. Set your own lines with the messages attribute.

title: Sampling pad
description: Two dials in one: temperature across, top-p up. The pixel field glows around the puck, leaves a fading trail and throws a ripple when you press. On release it springs onto the nearest 0.05.
tryText: **Try:** drag in circles, double-click to reset, or use the arrow keys.

title: Voice input
description: A mirrored pixel spectrum with falling peak dots, and words that drift into focus as they are recognised. Stopping collapses the bars into a line and the line into a point. The audio is simulated, since a shared page can’t use the microphone.

title: Materializing stream
description: Streamed text that condenses out of pixel dust. Every word arrives as a cloud of particles sampled from its own glyphs, springs into shape, then resolves into crisp type.
tryText: **Try:** replay it and watch the words land in the order they stream.

title: Model morph
description: One swarm of pixels takes a different shape per model: a sparse, jittery diamond for speed, a calm ring for balance, a dense rotating star for depth. Switching sends every pixel flying to its new place.

title: Secret field
description: The key hides under crawling pixel noise. Holding the eye wipes the noise away behind a dithered edge while each character decodes through random glyphs before it locks. Let go and it scrambles shut. The key shown is a fake.

title: Status orb
description: An agent’s state as a pixel disc: breathing when idle, ripples while listening, a spiral when thinking, an orbiting comet with a scanner while working, a glitching X on error, a check when done. States dissolve into each other pixel by pixel.

title: Fader & meter
description: A mixing-desk fader beside a stereo pixel meter, with peak-hold segments that hang and then fall. Push past 0 dB and the top turns red and the clip light fires.
tryText: **Try:** drag the cap up, double-click to snap to 0 dB, or mute.

title: Histogram range
description: A two-thumb filter over a pixel histogram. Columns that enter the range light up from the bottom like filling glasses, columns that leave drain away, and the run count rolls as you drag.

title: Focus timer
description: Sixty pixels make the ring. Each second the next one trembles, breaks loose and drops into a sand pile below. Reset and the whole pile flies back up into place.
tryText: **Try:** start it, let a few fall, then reset.

title: Slide to deploy
description: The Ultracode trail turned into a commit gesture. Sliding charges a pixel trail that heats up and starts to boil near the end. Release early and it drains back; reach the end and it bursts, scans and goes live.
tryText: **Try:** drag the arrow all the way, or focus it and press Enter.

title: Activity heatmap
description: Every day is a cell made of nine sub-pixels, so intensity shows as both brightness and density. Hovering draws a crosshair and a tooltip; clicking sends a ripple across the months; switching metric flips the cells in a diagonal wave.

title: Storage ring
description: A donut of pixels that sweeps in clockwise. Point at a segment, on the ring or in the legend, and its pixels push outward while the rest dim and the centre rolls to that category. Click to pin it.

title: Pixel avatar
description: A symmetric 7×7 avatar generated from a name. Every keystroke re-hashes it, and the cells that change flip over in a ring spreading from the centre while the hue drifts. Pixels near the pointer lift toward it.
tryText: **Try:** type your own name one letter at a time.

title: Latency scope
description: A scrolling oscilloscope where each sample is a bright head over a dithered tail. Spikes cross the 400 ms line in amber and red, and the readout rolls with p50 and p95 alongside.
tryText: **Try:** simulate an outage, then hover the trace to read any sample.

title: Pixel reactions
description: The heart’s pixels explode outward and snap back filled. Unliking drains it row by row to an outline. Press and hold for four more reactions; picking one sends the same pixels flying into its shape.

title: Pixel upload
description: The file icon dissolves from its corner, and each pixel arcs down into the progress bar. When it fills, the bar regroups into a check; files over the limit turn red and shake. Real files work too.
tryText: **Try:** both buttons, or drop a file onto the zone.

title: Charge to generate
description: Press and hold: pixels spiral in from the edges, the ring fills and the button starts to tremble. Let go and it fires a shockwave sized to how long you held, from one variation up to four.
tryText: **Try:** hold it for different lengths, or tap once to see it ask for more.

title: Pattern lock
description: Draw through the nodes to unlock. The trail is pixels, skipped middle nodes join automatically, a wrong pattern shatters and falls, and the right one goes green node by node.
tryText: **Try:** draw an L, or press Show me.

title: Pixel checklist
description: Checking a task fills its box from the centre, draws a check, then sends a strike-through across the text with a fizzing head. Finishing the list turns the bar green and runs a wave along it.

title: Level up
description: XP pours into a pixel bar with a hot leading edge. When it overflows, the bar flashes and the level number bursts into pixels that reassemble as the next one.
tryText: **Try:** press +180 a couple of times.

title: Dissolve to delete
description: Deleting a chat turns the row into its own pixels, sampled from the real text, and they drift away left to right before the gap closes.
tryText: **Try:** hover a row and press the bin, then Restore all.

title: Release rocket
description: A pixel rocket: a big countdown, smoke on the pad, then liftoff with a flame trail while the stars streak past. Land it again afterwards.

title: Day / night switch
description: The sun’s pixels fly apart and rebuild as a crescent moon while night sweeps across the sky and stars come out. In this demo it switches the theme of the whole page.

title: Pixel stars
description: Stars fill like liquid as you hover, column by column with a wave at the front. Picking one pops it with sparks and rolls the label.
tryText: **Try:** use 1 to 5 on the keyboard too.

title: Notification bell
description: A new notification swings the bell on its pivot with a lagging clapper, sends sound waves out both sides and pops the badge. Clicking the bell clears it in a spray of pixels.

title: Temperature fire
description: Model temperature as a real fire simulation. Low values leave embers, “Creative” burns tall, and “Wild” starts throwing sparks.
tryText: **Try:** drag across it, from 0.0 to 2.0.

title: Radio tuner
description: Drag the band to tune. Static thins out as you near a station, a waveform appears, and the station name resolves when it locks. Let go nearby and it springs onto the frequency.
tryText: **Try:** find OPUS FM at 101.1.

title: Equalizer
description: Seven bands on springs with a smooth curve drawn through them, over a live spectrum that reacts to the gains. Presets cascade band by band.
tryText: **Try:** drag a band, double-click to zero it.

title: Jog wheel
description: Spin the wheel and let go: it keeps turning with inertia, the timecode runs and the filmstrip scrubs underneath. Fast spins leave ghosted teeth.

title: Metronome
description: A swinging pixel pendulum whose weight slides with the tempo, four beat lamps and sparks at each extreme. Tap tempo works, and sound is off until you turn it on.

title: Pixel colour picker
description: A grid of colour pixels with a fisheye that swells cells under your pointer. Picking a hue sends the new colour rippling across the grid from where you clicked.

title: Mirror sketchpad
description: A 16×16 drawing pad with mirror mode, so every stroke is symmetric. Cells pop as you paint, and Clear drops every pixel off the bottom with gravity.

title: Context waffle
description: The context window as 200 cells, one per thousand tokens, grouped by source. Attaching a file flies new cells in and pushes the rest along; compacting crumbles the conversation and closes the gap.
tryText: **Try:** hover the legend to isolate a source.

title: LED ticker
description: An LED marquee: glowing text over a grid of unlit dots, coloured up and down arrows and soft edges. Hovering eases it to a stop rather than freezing it.

title: Service radar
description: A sweeping radar where each service lights up as the beam passes and fades over a revolution. Ping sends a ring out that flashes every node it touches.
tryText: **Try:** hover a blip for its latency.

title: Uptime history
description: Ninety days per service as pixel columns, swept in on load. Hovering a day lifts that column across every service and shows what happened.

title: Morphing clock
description: A live clock where every changing digit rolls to the next one and sheds a few pixels. Switching time zone rolls every digit at once.

title: Waveform player
description: A pixel waveform that fills as it plays, previews ahead of the playhead on hover and sends a ripple out from wherever you click. The track is silent.

title: Request globe
description: A dotted sphere with nine regions. Requests arc between them as glowing packets, each arrival flashes the node and rolls the counter. Drag to spin it.

title: Code minimap
description: A syntax-coloured pixel minimap beside a code file, with the visible window outlined. Search results pulse in the margin; drag the minimap to scroll.
tryText: **Try:** press Enter in the search box to jump between matches.

title: Diffusion preview
description: An image generating the way diffusion models work: noise and big blocks that sharpen step by step into a scene. Three prompts, and every variation is different.

title: Snake stepper
description: Onboarding progress as a pixel snake. It idles in a loop around the current step, slithers along the path to the next one, eats it and grows.
tryText: **Try:** go to the end and press Finish.

title: Pixel loaders
description: Six loading indicators made of pixels: orbit, snake, helix, scan, rain and pulse. Clicking one finishes it with a check before it starts again.

title: Typing heatmap
description: A typing test over a pixel keyboard. Each key flashes and ripples to its neighbours, builds up heat the more you use it, and turns red on a miss.

title: Token view
description: Type and the text splits into tokens, shown as tinted spans and as a strip of pixels where new tokens drop in. The tokenizer is a rough approximation.
tryText: **Try:** hover a token in either view.

title: Usage battery
description: Weekly usage as a pixel battery. Spending knocks cells loose so they float off; resetting runs current in along the cable with a pulsing bolt until it’s full.

title: Text field
description: A labelled field whose underline lights up from the caret outwards. Validation runs on blur: an invalid value shakes the field, scatters the pixels and rolls in the message; a valid one draws a check.
tryText: **Try:** type half an email address, then click away.
markup: <px-input name="email" label="Work email" type="email" required placeholder="you@example.com" hint="We’ll send the invite here" error="Enter a valid email address"></px-input>

title: Password
description: A pixel strength meter in four segments, a show/hide toggle and a checklist whose bullets pop as each rule is met. With `minScore` set, weaker passwords block form submission.

title: One-time code
description: Six boxes backed by one real input, so typing, pasting and the phone’s one-time-code autofill all work. Digits rise into their boxes; a wrong code shakes and falls away.
tryText: **Try:** type 424242, then something else.

title: Search with results
description: Fuzzy matching with highlighted letters, a scanning line while it searches and a pixel highlight that springs between results. With `hotkey`, “/” focuses it from anywhere.
tryText: **Try:** press / and type “bil”, then use the arrow keys.

title: Select
description: Takes a typed list of options. The menu unfolds downward, a pixel highlight follows your pointer or the arrow keys, and typing a letter jumps to it.
markup:
<px-select name="model" label="Model" hint="You can change this per chat">
  <option value="large" data-desc="Most capable">Large</option>
  <option value="medium" data-desc="Balanced" selected>Medium</option>
  <option value="small" data-desc="Fastest">Small</option>
</px-select>

title: Slider
description: A general slider with a pixel track, a springy thumb, optional tick marks and a rolling value with prefix or unit.
markup: <px-slider name="budget" label="Monthly budget" min="0" max="500" step="10" value="120" prefix="€" ticks></px-slider>

title: Checkbox
description: Fills from the centre and draws its check, and supports the mixed state. This demo wires an “All channels” parent to three children.
stage: Notify me byAll channelsEmailPushSMS

title: Option cards
description: A radio group as cards. The selection outline is made of pixels that fly from the old card to the new one, then keep circling slowly.
tryText: **Try:** use the arrow keys.
stage:
<px-choice name="plan" label="Plan">
  <option value="free" data-desc="For trying things out" data-price="€0">Free</option>
  <option value="pro" data-desc="For daily work" data-price="€20/mo" selected>Pro</option>
  <option value="team" data-desc="Shared projects" data-price="€30/user">Team</option>
</px-choice>
markup:
<px-choice name="plan" label="Plan">
  <option value="free" data-desc="For trying things out" data-price="€0">Free</option>
  <option value="pro" data-desc="For daily work" data-price="€20/mo" selected>Pro</option>
  <option value="team" data-desc="Shared projects" data-price="€30/user">Team</option>
</px-choice>

title: Tag input
description: Enter or comma adds a tag, Backspace on an empty field marks the last one and a second press removes it. Removed tags break into pixels; duplicates shake instead of being added.

title: Date picker
description: A month grid with a pixel selection block that springs between days, a dotted band across ranges and a mark on today. Weeks start on Monday; leave out `range` for a single date.
tryText: **Try:** arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month.

title: Text area with budget
description: Grows with its content and shows the character budget as pixels that turn amber near the limit. Going over is allowed but blinks red and marks the form invalid.
markup: <px-textarea name="bio" label="Short bio" limit="120" placeholder="A sentence or two about you"></px-textarea>

title: Async button
description: Return a promise from `onClick` (or pass an async function to `run()` on its ref) and it shows a pixel spinner, then a drawn check or a shake with “Try again”. Inside a form, `type="submit"` submits it.
tryText: **Try:** both buttons run a fake 1.3-second task; the second one fails.
markup:
<px-button id="save">Save changes</px-button>
<script>
  save.addEventListener('click', () => save.run(() => fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST' })));
</script>

title: Two-step delete
description: The first click arms it and a pixel fuse burns down along the bottom. A second click inside the window confirms with a burst; Escape, blur or the timeout cancel it.

title: Toasts
description: Stacked notifications with pixel icons and a draining timer that pauses while you hover or focus the stack. Add `position="bottom-right"` to pin it to the viewport.
markup:
<px-toaster id="toasts" position="bottom-right"></px-toaster>
<script>
  toasts.show({ title: 'Saved', desc: 'Settings updated', type: 'success' });
  toasts.show({ title: '3 files deleted', type: 'info', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } });
</script>

title: Progress bar
description: Determinate with a hot leading edge and a green sweep when it finishes, or indeterminate (no value) as a moving comet.
markup:
<px-progress value="40" label="Uploading dataset"></px-progress>
<px-progress label="Indexing"></px-progress>   <!-- no value: indeterminate -->

title: Progress ring
description: A circular version with the percentage counting up in its centre. It turns green and throws a few sparks at 100%.
stage: Weekly usageSyncing

title: Loading skeleton
description: Wraps real content and shows shimmering pixel bars in its shape while loading. Turning `loading` off dissolves the skeleton as the content fades in.
stage:
Ada Lovelace
Shared “Notes on the Analytical Engine” in Research. 3 comments, 12 reactions.

title: Empty state
description: Four pixel illustrations that drop into place and float gently, with a title, a line of help and room for actions.
markup:
<px-empty kind="inbox" heading="No messages yet" text="New messages will show up here.">
  <button>Compose</button>
</px-empty>

title: Inline alert
description: Info, success, warning and error, each with a pixel icon and a glowing stripe. Dismissing scatters the stripe and collapses the alert.
stage: The large model is now the default for new chats.You’ve used most of this week’s limit.We couldn’t reach Google Drive. Check the connection.
markup: <px-alert type="warning" heading="Usage at 85%" dismissible>You’ve used most of this week’s limit.</px-alert>

title: Tooltip
description: The bubble grows out of its arrow pixel by pixel on hover or keyboard focus, then the text fades in. Escape hides it.
tryText: **Try:** tab onto the buttons.

title: Avatar
description: Initials on a pixel field coloured from the name, so the same person always gets the same colour. Status dots pulse when online, and hovering sends a ripple through the field.

title: Tabs
description: The underline is forty pixels that stream from the old tab to the new one. Each item brings its own panel content.
stage:
Usage is steady this week. Most runs come from the Research project.
12 events since Monday, including 3 deploys and 2 new members.
Default model, retention and notification settings live here.
markup:
<px-tabs>
  <section data-tab="Overview">Usage is steady this week. Most runs come from the Research project.</section>
  <section data-tab="Activity" data-count="12">12 events since Monday, including 3 deploys and 2 new members.</section>
  <section data-tab="Settings">Default model, retention and notification settings live here.</section>
</px-tabs>

title: Pagination
description: Page buttons with ellipses, where the current-page block slides to the page you pick.

title: Sidebar nav
description: Takes a list of links and adds pixel icons, count badges, a soft hover block and an active bar that slides to the current item.
stage: Home Chats Projects Usage Team Settings
markup: Home Chats Projects Usage Team Settings

title: Accordion
description: Pixel plus signs fold into minus signs, panels open smoothly and a dotted rail marks the open answer. Set `multiple` to allow several open at once.
stage:
A mode that sends xhigh effort and lets the agent plan multi-agent workflows on its own.
Usage resets weekly. Longer reasoning and more agents use more of it.
Yes. Settings has an export that includes chats, projects and files.
markup:
<px-accordion>
  <section data-title="What is Ultracode?" data-open>A mode that sends xhigh effort and lets the agent plan multi-agent workflows on its own.</section>
  <section data-title="How is usage counted?">Usage resets weekly. Longer reasoning and more agents use more of it.</section>
  <section data-title="Can I export my data?">Yes. Settings has an export that includes chats, projects and files.</section>
</px-accordion>

title: Command menu
description: A ⌘K / Ctrl+K palette with grouped commands, fuzzy search and a springing pixel highlight. It traps focus while open and returns it to where it was on close.
tryText: **Try:** press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac).

title: Wizard steps
description: Numbered nodes joined by pixel lines that fill as you advance. Finished steps show a check and can be clicked to go back.

title: Sparkline
description: An inline pixel line with a dithered area, coloured by trend unless you set a colour. Hovering shows the value under the pointer.
stage:
Requests58k
Errors0.3%
Latency222 ms

title: Bar chart
description: Bars stacked from pixel cells that grow in one after another and spring to new data. Hover or use the arrow keys for exact values.

title: Stat tile
description: A metric with a rolling value, a change chip and a pixel history. Set `invert` when lower is better, so a drop shows green.

title: Button
description: Noise-lit surface, pointer light, ripples on press, a flowing loading field and a sweep on success. `run(fn)` takes a promise and handles all three states.
tryText: **Try:** click both: one succeeds, one fails.
stage: GenerateDelete

title: Switch
description: The track charges up with a dithered energy field when it turns on and the thumb springs across with a few sparks. Form-associated, like every control here.
stage: UltracodePlan multi-agent workflowsWeb searchLook things up while answering
markup: UltracodePlan multi-agent workflowsWeb searchLook things up while answering

title: Segmented control
description: The selected slab is liquid: it stretches toward the new option on a spring and settles with a glint.
tryText: **Try:** use the arrow keys.

title: Text field
description: A comet of light runs around the border while you type and sparks off the caret. Invalid input turns the border into static; a valid value gets a green sweep.
tryText: **Try:** type half an email address, then click away.
markup: <hf-input name="email" label="Work email" type="email" required placeholder="you@example.com" hint="We’ll send the invite here"></hf-input>

title: Prompt composer
description: A chat input whose border is an aurora of dots. The effort chip cycles through levels and the band gets brighter with each step; sending launches a wave from right to left and fires a `send` event with the text and effort.
tryText: **Try:** type something and press Enter, or click the effort chip.
markup: <hf-composer effort="ultracode" placeholder="Ask the agent to build something…"></hf-composer>

title: Slider
description: A dithered fill with a lens for a thumb: the dots under it are magnified, so you can see the exact position.
markup: <hf-slider name="temp" label="Temperature" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.7"></hf-slider>

title: Knob
description: A dithered sphere with an arc of lit cells. Drag around the dial, scroll, or use the arrow keys; the value rolls in below.
tryText: **Try:** drag around the dial or scroll over it.
stage: <hf-knob name="gain" label="Gain" min="0" max="12" step="0.5" value="7" unit=" dB" style="zoom:.8"></hf-knob>
markup: <hf-knob name="gain" label="Gain" min="0" max="12" step="0.5" value="7" unit=" dB"></hf-knob>

title: Drop zone
description: The surface is a small wave simulation: dragging a file over it raises ripples under the pointer, dropping makes a splash, and each file gets a dotted progress bar.
tryText: **Try:** drag a file onto it, or click to browse.

title: Pricing
description: Switching billing period rolls the price to the new number while a bright edge wipes through the dot grid behind it.
tryText: **Try:** switch between Monthly and Yearly.

title: Shortcut keys
description: Keycaps drawn in dots, with the key names set in type, that light up and press down when you hold the real keys, and fire a `trigger` event when the whole combination is down.
tryText: **Try:** hold Shift and press Enter.

title: Progress
description: A fluid fill with rising bubbles and a meniscus at the front; at 100% the label rolls to its done text and the fluid flashes. Leave out `value` for an indeterminate blob.

title: Context window
description: Your favourite, rebuilt in HD: four segments with dithered boundaries, warnings at 80% and 95%, and a compaction sweep that squeezes the conversation back down. Hover the legend to isolate a segment.
tryText: **Try:** add messages until it warns, then compact.

title: Gauge
description: A semicircle of green, amber and red cells with a sprung pointer and a shimmer in the filled part. Past the last zone it pulses. The status word rolls when the zone changes.

title: Goal rings
description: Three progress rings with glowing heads. Going past the goal laps the ring in a brighter colour and throws sparks at the top. Hover a ring or a legend row to isolate it.

title: Uptime
description: Daily bars that rise in from the left, coloured by incidents, with today pulsing. Hover or use the arrow keys for the day’s numbers; the number of days adapts to the width.
tryText: **Try:** hover the red bar.

title: Terminal
description: A small simulated shell: type `help`, `test`, `deploy` or `ultracode`. Output lines flash like phosphor, progress bars are drawn in dots and the block caret glows.
tryText: **Try:** type ultracode and press Enter.

title: Countdown
description: Each digit sits on its own dotted tile; when it changes, the digit rolls over and a bright line prints through the tile from top to bottom. The last ten seconds turn red, and zero bursts.

title: Announcement
description: A dithered gradient with a passing sheen and a twinkling sparkle. Dismissing it disintegrates it into dots that blow away to the right before the space closes.
tryText: **Try:** press the ✕.
stage: Ultracode is herePlan and run multi-agent workflows from the composer.
markup: Ultracode is here Plan and run multi-agent workflows from the composer.

title: Effort slider
description: Same rules as the first one: below Ultracode it is a plain slider. At Ultracode it bursts, and a trail of light grows from the thumb toward the left, stopping three quarters along, with pulses running right to left. The level name rolls like a picker wheel.
tryText: **Try:** drag it to the far right.

title: Mode picker
description: Three option cards on one canvas. The selected card gets an aurora and a comet that runs around its border; Ultracode switches the aurora to a full spectrum, adds twinkles and bursts when picked.
tryText: **Try:** pick Ultracode.

title: Agent run
description: Steps with a spinning arc while running, a check carved out of a disc when done, and light flowing down the connector into the next step. Header shows elapsed time and tokens.
tryText: **Try:** press Run again.

title: Streaming reply
description: Each token resolves out of a patch of noise as it arrives, a glowing block caret rides the end of the text, and a dotted sparkline tracks tokens per second.
tryText: **Try:** press Stop, then Regenerate.

title: Area chart
description: A bright line over a dithered fill that thins toward the bottom. Ranges morph into each other; hovering adds a crosshair, a bloom on the point and the value in the header.
tryText: **Try:** switch to 90D, then hover.

title: Donut
description: Sweeps in clockwise. Hovering a segment or legend row pops it outward and rolls its share into the middle; arrow keys work too.

title: Stat tile
description: The number counts up over a shimmer of dots; hovering the sparkline swaps it for the value under the pointer.

title: Funnel
description: Dots fall through the stages in proportion to conversion; the ones that drop out turn red and drift off the side.

title: Bar list
description: Ranked rows with dithered bars behind the labels. They grow in one after another, and hovering a row runs a sheen along its bar.

title: Media card
description: A procedurally drawn landscape whose ridges move at different depths as the card tilts toward your pointer, with a glare of dots following it.
stage: Pixel ValleyA generated landscape that drifts with your pointer. Every layer is a dithered noise ridge.
markup: Pixel ValleyA generated landscape that drifts with your pointer. Every layer is a dithered noise ridge.

title: Hero
description: The headline is revealed from left to right behind a bright front, then a shimmer runs through the dots around it. Your pointer pushes the dots aside and a click sends a shockwave through them.
tryText: **Try:** move through the headline and click.
markup: <hf-hero headline="Think in pixels." primary="Get started" secondary="View components"></hf-hero>

title: Secret field
description: The value sits under live static. Revealing dissolves the noise outward from where you clicked; it hides itself again after fifteen seconds, and Copy flashes green.
tryText: **Try:** click into the field.

title: Time picker wheel
description: A picker wheel like the one in the effort slider’s name, turned into a full control. Rows curve away on a cylinder, the selection band magnifies, and it flings with inertia before snapping to a value.
tryText: **Try:** drag or scroll a column, or use the arrow keys.
markup: <hf-wheel name="remind" label="Remind me at" value="09:30" step="5"></hf-wheel>

title: Range filter
description: Two thumbs over a dithered histogram. Bars inside the range light up, the result count rolls, and the min and max fields stay in sync both ways.
tryText: **Try:** drag either thumb or type a value.
markup: <hf-range name="price" label="Price per month" min="0" max="500" step="5" low="100" high="350"></hf-range>

title: Filter chips
description: Selecting a chip floods it with dots from where you clicked and draws a pixel check; Clear empties them all. Submits one form value per selected chip.

title: Number stepper
description: The number rolls up or down over a dotted wash, and a scan line crosses the dots on every step. Hold a button to repeat faster, with heat and sparks building up; bumping the limit flashes red. Click the number to type.
tryText: **Try:** hold the plus button.
markup: <hf-number name="seats" label="Seats" value="12" min="1" max="50" price="24"></hf-number>

title: Slide to confirm
description: For actions that shouldn’t happen by accident. A sheen runs across the label, the track fills behind the handle, and reaching the end bursts and confirms. Keyboard users hold Enter instead.
tryText: **Try:** drag the handle all the way.

title: PIN pad
description: Keys ripple when pressed, dots pop in with bloom, a wrong code turns them to red static and shakes, and the right one sends a green wave. Your keyboard works too.
tryText: **Try:** try a wrong PIN first.

title: Split button
description: A primary action with a menu of alternatives. Rows sweep in, a highlight springs between them, and choosing one rolls it into the main button.
tryText: **Try:** open the menu and pick “Create preview”.
markup: <hf-split items="Deploy to production|Ships to everyone;Deploy to staging|Internal testers only"></hf-split>

title: @mention field
description: Type @ for files, people and agents. Suggestions filter as you type with matched letters marked; inserted mentions become dotted chips that flash in.
tryText: **Try:** type “@re” and press Enter.

title: Permission prompt
description: A scan runs across the command, then a risk meter fills. High-risk commands can’t be always-allowed. Deciding sweeps the card green or fills it with red static. Keys 1–3 answer.
tryText: **Try:** click through the queue with “Next request”.

title: Diff review
description: Takes a unified diff as its text content. Added and removed lines get dithered tints and a minimap on the right; accepting a hunk dissolves the dropped lines to the right.
tryText: **Try:** accept one hunk and reject the other.
markup:
<hf-diff>
--- a/src/auth/session.ts
+++ b/src/auth/session.ts
@@ -12,7 +12,9 @@ export async function refresh(session) {
-  return login();
+  return rotate(token);
</hf-diff>

title: Changed files
description: Builds a tree from a list of paths with M/A/D markers. Pixel icons take the status colour, folders count their changes and the selection springs between rows. Full tree keyboard support.
tryText: **Try:** use the arrow keys, or “Changed only”.

title: Agent graph
description: Ultracode’s lead agent hands off to a planner, three agents in parallel and a reviewer. Live edges stream light with packets, running nodes get a comet halo, and narrow screens switch to a vertical layout.
tryText: **Try:** press Run.

title: PII redaction
description: Finds names, emails, IBANs and phone numbers and shows what the model would see instead. Placeholders resolve out of noise; switching off dissolves the chips back to the original text. Edit the text to try your own.
tryText: **Try:** type another email address.

title: Checkpoints
description: Scrub back through a session. Each jump runs a rewind glitch over the code before it swaps, and lines that changed get a green bar.
tryText: **Try:** drag the head to “Start” and back.

title: Sources and citations
description: Hovering a citation draws a dotted beam to its source chip with packets running along it. The preview loads with a pixel skeleton, and each favicon is the domain's first letter on a dotted tile.
tryText: **Try:** hover the numbers in the text.

title: Usage heatmap
description: Weekday by hour. Each cell is a block of dots whose density is the value; the peak pulses, hovering adds a crosshair and the metrics morph into each other.
tryText: **Try:** switch to Tokens, then hover.

title: Scatter with brush
description: 270 runs that settle in, glowing where they cluster. Drag a box to select and the summary rolls to the selection’s medians; the legend toggles models.
tryText: **Try:** drag a box around the green cluster.

title: Candlesticks
description: Live OHLC with dithered bodies, wicks, volume and a dotted last-price line. The last candle ticks and a new one opens every few seconds with a flash.
tryText: **Try:** hover a candle for its values.

title: Flow
description: A sankey from surfaces to models, with particles streaming along each band in proportion to its traffic. Hover a band to isolate it.

title: Roadmap
description: Bars fill with progress dither, the launch milestone pulses and the today line has a glint travelling down it. Drag to reschedule or resize, snapping by day.
tryText: **Try:** drag “Security review” a week later.

title: Live leaderboard
description: Scores tick up live; when a team overtakes another, rows slide past each other with green and red trails and the ranks roll. The leader gets a gold ring.
tryText: **Try:** watch for an overtake, or press Live to pause.

title: Radial bars
description: Twelve months around a dial, filled denser toward the tip. The current month pulses; hovering rolls its value into the middle and years morph.
tryText: **Try:** switch to 2025.

title: Logo marquee
description: Two rows of placeholder wordmarks drifting in opposite directions between dotted rules, faded at the edges. The row under your pointer slows and the wordmark under it lights up on a dotted plate.

title: Dialog
description: A real modal dialog: it traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus. Opening it, its pixels fly out of the button and assemble the panel over a dithered backdrop; closing sends them back.
tryText: **Try:** open it, then press Escape.

title: Kanban board
description: Drag cards between columns: a trail of dots follows, the target column lights up and a bar shows where it will land. Dropping into Done bursts. Arrow keys move the focused card.
tryText: **Try:** drag a card into Done.

title: Carousel
description: Four procedural scenes. Slides change with an ordered-dither dissolve and a bright front, autoplay pauses on hover or focus, and it swipes.
tryText: **Try:** use the arrows or swipe.

title: Product tour
description: Dims the interface with dither, cuts a rounded hole around each step’s target with a comet on its edge, and springs between steps.
tryText: **Try:** take the tour.

title: Privacy choices
description: The shield fills as you allow more categories. Saving stamps it with a ring and the card folds into a small “Change” pill.
tryText: **Try:** switch on Analytics, then Save.

title: Error state
description: The code sits in large mono type inside a halo of dotted scanlines. It slips into a glitch now and then (more when your pointer is near), and Try again scatters the halo while the code blurs back in.
tryText: **Try:** press Try again.

title: Before and after
description: A document before and after redaction, split by a draggable handle. Works with the arrow keys too.
tryText: **Try:** drag the handle.

title: Connection globe
description: A dotted globe of the land masses with a hairline coastline. Each connection is a dotted arc that rises higher the farther it travels, with a packet at its head. When the packet lands, the land dots around the destination light up in an uneven ring and a few sparks fly off past the edge of the globe.

Drag to turn the globe; it coasts and settles. Locations are buttons over the canvas: Tab and the arrow keys move between them, focusing one turns the globe toward it, and selecting one keeps only its connections lit. Pass `connections` for your own data, or call `push()` on the ref for a live feed.
tryText: **Try:** drag the globe and let go, then select a location and send a burst to it.

title: Horizon globe
description: The top of a large dotted globe rising from the bottom edge, for page heroes. On first view the horizon line draws out from its middle and the land appears behind an uneven, bright front that spreads from the same point.

Then connections leave the surface, climb into the sky above the horizon and come down in another region, where a ring of dots lights up, while a glint runs along the limb now and then. Your headline and actions are regular children over the sky. The globe drifts slowly while it is in view.
tryText: **Try:** scroll the hero out of view and back; the reveal plays once, the arcs continue.

title: Day and night
description: A dotted globe split by the terminator. The twilight band is drawn with an ordered dither, so day thins into night dot by dot, and city lights shine on the night side.
Scrub up to 12 hours either way: as night reaches a city its lights switch on one after another with a small flash, and at dawn they go out. The UTC time and the offset roll as you drag.
tryText: **Try:** drag the time slider or press Play 24 h, and watch the lights come on along the terminator. Drag the globe to turn it.

title: Event spikes
description: Counts per location as spikes of stacked dots standing on a dotted globe. Heights use a log scale by default, so one busy city does not flatten the rest.

When the data changes, spikes grow on springs in a wave that starts at the location with the biggest increase and spreads around the globe, with a ring of light on the land marking the front. Point at a spike, or Tab to it, to roll its count.
tryText: **Try:** press Refresh and watch the growth spread from the biggest change.

title: Globe to map
description: One set of land dots that is either a globe or a flat map. Switching peels the globe open at the back: dots near the seam swing out first and the hidden side comes around the edges as it turns toward you. When the cut edges land, light runs along them; closing folds the middle first.
Routes between regions bend from lifted arcs on the globe to flat curves on the map, with packets running along them in both views.
tryText: **Try:** drag the globe first so the seam moves, then switch to Map.

title: Region badge
description: A pill with a tiny dotted globe, a region name and its latency, for headers, footers and status bars. The globe shows where the region is.

When the region changes, the globe turns to it on a slightly under-damped spring, overshoots a little and settles, then a ring of light pings across its dots and throws a few sparks past the edge. The name rolls in the direction of the turn and each digit of the latency rolls to the new value.
tryText: **Try:** press Switch region a few times, or click the top badge.

title: Marker map
description: A flat map of land dots with markers. Markers with a value grow a halo of lit dots sized by that value, so the busiest places read at a glance without circles drawn over the map.
Halos grow and shrink behind an uneven front when values change, markers can pulse as rings of light, and labels place themselves so they do not overlap.
tryText: **Try:** press Shuffle values and watch the halos spring to their new sizes, then select a marker, or tab to the map and move between markers with the arrow keys.

title: Live visitors
description: A live map of visits with a feed beside it and an online-now count. Each visit drops onto the map and lands with a splash of light and a few sparks that can fly past the map's edge, while its row slides into the feed.
Visits leave an afterglow on the land dots that fades over five minutes, so busy regions build up a soft density. Pointing at a row highlights its point, and pointing at a point highlights its row.
tryText: **Try:** press Burst, then point at a row in the feed and at a glowing area on the map.

title: Region traffic
description: Traffic between regions as dotted curves whose width and particle rate follow throughput. Downstream runs in the accent colour and upstream in the info colour, each bending to its own side of the line.
Select a region and its flows stay lit while all others collapse to hairlines and drain; the inbound and outbound totals roll to that region's numbers.
tryText: **Try:** select a region, then press Escape to see every flow again.

title: Country values
description: Values per country shown as dot density: each country's land dots switch on in an ordered-dither pattern, so a higher class reads as a denser print. Countries without data stay as the plain base.

When the data changes, each country builds up or thins out dot by dot in dither order, outward from its middle behind a bright front. Pointing at a country sends a short light around its border and rolls its value, and a ranked list beside the map stays in sync.
tryText: **Try:** switch the metric, then point at a country.

title: Clustered map
description: A zoomable map for many points. Nearby points merge into clusters with a count; zooming in splits each cluster into its children, which spring out from where the parent was, and zooming out pulls them back together while the counts roll.
The land dots are re-sampled at the same pixel pitch for every zoom level, so coastlines sharpen as you zoom. Use Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel, pinch, double-click, or the + and − buttons.
tryText: **Try:** click a large cluster to split it, then zoom back out with the − button.

title: Location cell
description: A 96 × 48 world thumbnail with one point, sized for table cells and list rows.

Hover or focus it and a popover grows out of the point while the map inside dives toward it: finer land resolves outward from the point and a ring of dots pings where it lands. The place name, coordinates, local time and an optional distance appear as text. Thumbnails of one size share one baked lattice, so a table full of them stays light.
tryText: **Try:** move the pointer down the location column, then click a map to pin its card.

title: Anycast catchment
description: Which point of presence serves which part of the world. Every land dot belongs to its nearest active site, the borders between catchments are drawn brighter, and the selected site's area is lit in the accent colour. Point at the map to see which site serves that spot and the estimated round trip.

Turn a site off to simulate an outage: its area drops out in a wave from the site, then the neighbouring sites flood the hole, each front starting at its own side. Turn it back on and it reclaims its area from its centre. Request shares roll to the new numbers, and a dotted strip shows every site's share of the traffic.
tryText: **Try:** turn Frankfurt off and watch its neighbours take over.

title: Mesh connections
description: The devices of a private network and how this device reaches each of them: directly, or through a relay server when a direct path cannot be opened. Relayed connections run as two legs through the relay; direct ones as a single line, with traffic moving both ways.

When a relayed connection becomes direct, two probes meet in the middle, the path lets go of the relay and straightens with a slight wobble, and the latency rolls down to the new value. A connection that falls back to a relay bends back through it.
tryText: **Try:** press Reconnect all and watch the paths let go of their relays one by one.

title: Traceroute
description: A traceroute as a hop table and a map. The path draws hop by hop, and the packet waits at each hop for its share of the round-trip time, so slow hops are slow to watch.

Jumps of more than 40 ms are drawn as dashed long-haul segments with the added time beside them. Hops without a location, or that did not answer, stay in the table only. Selecting a row highlights its segment.
tryText: **Try:** press Replay, then move through the table with the arrow keys.

title: Latency matrix
description: Round-trip times between regions as a grid of dot blocks: the slower the pair, the more dots are lit. Pairs above a threshold get a warning mark.

Point at a cell, or move through the grid with the arrow keys, and the mini map beside it shows that pair: the measured route against a faint arc for the fibre minimum, with the milliseconds and the path stretch rolling. The route slides from pair to pair instead of redrawing.
tryText: **Try:** hold an arrow key in the grid and watch the route slide across the map.

title: Global checks
description: Uptime checks from many locations against one target. Each round, every probe fires at the same moment and the arcs race to the target; each arrives after its own measured time, so the order they land in is the latency ranking.

As each result lands, its row slides into place in the ranked list and the median and 95th percentile roll. A failed check breaks off halfway with red sparks, and its row drops to the bottom as a timeout.
tryText: **Try:** press Run check and watch the list sort itself as results land.

title: Distance from here
description: A round map that puts one place at the centre and every other place at its true distance and direction from it. Dotted rings mark every 2,000 km, or every 50 ms of round-trip time, and the outer edge is the point on the other side of the world.

Pick another place and the map re-centres there: every dot moves to its new position, starting with those nearest the new centre, so the map grows outward from it. The distances in the list roll to their new values.
tryText: **Try:** pick Sydney, then switch the rings to latency.

title: Sign-in travel
description: An account's sign-ins in order, joined by lines on a map, with the speed each move would have needed. A move faster than travel allows is flagged as impossible.

A flagged leg tears: its line splits in the middle, the halves pull apart, red sparks crackle in the gap and a chip shows the speed, such as 16,272 km/h. The list beside the map shows the time and distance between sign-ins. Locations from IP addresses are approximate, so short jumps are never flagged.
tryText: **Try:** select the first Singapore sign-in to bring the torn leg forward, then press Replay.

title: Attack origins
description: Inbound requests from around the world converge on one protected site at the centre of a globe; requests from the far side come up over the horizon. A ring of dots around the site is its shield: blocked requests hit the ring and burst off it, allowed requests pass through and land.

Where a request hits, the shield dents and lights up for a moment. Counts per verdict and the top origin regions roll beside the globe; arcs in flight are capped and the rest are folded into the counts.
tryText: **Try:** press Flood and watch the shield take the hits.

title: Geofence
description: Allowed zones as true geodesic circles on a flat map, with tracked devices inside them. Drag a zone's centre to move it and the handle on its edge to resize it; the circle keeps its real shape, so it stretches toward the poles.
When a device leaves every zone, the fence it crossed rings like a plucked string: a wave runs around the circle from the crossing point in both directions, and the device turns to a warning colour.
tryText: **Try:** drag a zone away from a device, or shrink it until one falls outside.

title: Active sessions
description: The places an account is signed in, as a list with a compact map above it. Each row shows the device type, the city and when it was last active; pointing at a row pulses its point and draws a line from this device to it.
Sign out other sessions sends a wave across the map from this device. As it reaches each session, the point breaks up into sparks and its row collapses at the same moment, nearest first.
tryText: **Try:** press Sign out other sessions, then confirm.

title: Data residency
description: Where data is stored and processed, measured against a jurisdiction. The zone's land is lit, sites are marked inside or outside it, and transfers between sites are drawn as lines with data moving along them.

Transfers that stay inside the zone run quietly. When data on a transfer crosses the zone's border, the crossing point flares and the part outside turns into a dashed warning line; a chip counts the transfers that leave the zone.
tryText: **Try:** turn on Send analytics to us-east and watch where it crosses the border.

title: IP lookup
description: A field that looks up where an IP address is located and shows the result on a small map. While the lookup runs, a crosshair hops from land dot to land dot and slows down like a slot machine before it locks onto the result.

The coordinates roll into place, and the place, network and accuracy appear below. Private and reserved addresses are answered at once without a lookup. Bring your own `resolve` function; the built-in one invents a location and is only for demos.

title: Region picker
description: Pick a deployment region from a list with a map above it. The selection reticle travels to the new region along the great-circle path with a comet tail, and the land dots under it are magnified as it passes.
Give it a `from` location and every region shows an estimated round trip, with a dotted line from that location to the region you point at. It submits with forms through a hidden input.
tryText: **Try:** use the arrow keys: Up and Down follow the list, Left and Right jump west or east on the map.

title: Location picker
description: Choose a point on a map. Click or tap to drop the pin, search for a place, or type exact coordinates into the latitude and longitude fields.

The pin drops on a bouncy spring and lands with a splash: the dots around it are pushed outward in a ring like water, and the coordinates roll to the new values. Picking a search result flies the map there and zooms in so you can place the pin precisely.
tryText: **Try:** search for Lagos, then click next to it to move the pin.

title: Area select
description: Draw a rectangle of latitude and longitude on a map to select an area, for example to filter events by place. Move it, resize it from its edges and corners, type exact bounds, or double-click a country to fit the box to it.

While you draw, the land inside fills behind the pointer with a bright, uneven front, the dotted border runs, and the count of points inside rolls. On release the edges snap to whole degrees on springs. The box can cross the date line and continue on the other side of the map.
tryText: **Try:** drag the box east past the right edge of the map, then double-click Japan.

title: Coordinate field
description: A text field for coordinates that reads the usual ways of writing them: decimal degrees, degrees with minutes and seconds, hemisphere letters, or a signed pair. A small world map beside it shows what it read.

The map has a parallel and a meridian on separate springs: typing the latitude moves the horizontal line, the longitude moves the vertical one, and when both are read the crossing locks with a ping. Below the field the coordinates appear in the other format, with hemisphere letters that flip over when the sign changes.
tryText: **Try:** type 35°41′22″N 139°41′30″E, then change N to S.

title: Meeting planner
description: Several cities on one time line, one row per city, with each hour drawn as a block of dots: dense for working hours, sparse for the night. Drag the cursor across the rows and every city's local time rolls with it.

Hours when every city is at work light up as a band across all rows, and a light runs down the band when the cursor enters it. Offsets come from the time zone database, so daylight saving time is handled.
tryText: **Try:** drag the cursor into the lit band, then add Singapore.

title: Route playback
description: Replays a recorded track on a map fitted to it. The marker turns along its heading and leaves a wake of dots that cools behind it; stops leave a ring of dots that fills while the track waits there.

Play, pause and scrub at one hour, six hours or a day of track time per second. A speed chart under the map follows the playhead and scrubs too, and the time, speed and distance roll as the marker moves.
tryText: **Try:** scrub the speed chart back to the slow Suez passage after Port Said and press Play.
